text:
sara: incident-bot fired for chat-completions p99 across us-west-2 at 1718246400 :rotating_light:
incident-bot: ALERT: route=chat.completions.us-west-2 p99_latency > 1.8s for 5m (threshold=1.8s). paging @eng-sre oncall
mike: I’m on it, grabbing traces + tailing router logs
lee: I see a surge of long requests hitting the kv-cache miss path for model=mistral-8x. p95 stable but p99 spike. count of kv-cache misses up ~5x
anya: customer impact? any errors or primarily slow responses?
sara: at surface level ~10 customer-reported slow responses in the last 10m. no 5xx spikes in app layer, just latency.
mike: pulling batching stats. looks like batching window increased due to queueing when backend pods hit saturated GPU FPU. suspects model queuing on dedicated nodes
lee: adding a temporary route tweak: prefer model=mistral-8x-quant when latency > 1.2s and traffic < 2rps/customer. will push as a routing policy change for 5m as mitigation.
sara: create a short-lived canary route? we should avoid sudden quality regressions for customers.
anya: can we fallback to smaller model only for non-critical routes? Which routes are we talking about?
mike: route id: chat.completions.default-worker. I’ll create a policy: if p95>1.2s then route 20% to mistral-8x-quant and 80% to mistral-8x (soft fallback). testing locally.
ops-bot: /route-change applied: chat.completions.default-worker -> split policy (20% mistral-8x-quant) by user-group=nonpaid. Change id: rc-1718246450
lee: after split, p99 dropped from ~2.1s to ~1.6s within 90s. p95 unchanged. good sign
sara: paging: do we want to squelch p99 pager while mitigation active? we’ll still alert channel.
mike: propose squelch for 10m with escalations enabled. we’ll keep a lower fidelity p95 alert live.
anya: agree. set p99 squelch only for route=chat.completions.default-worker, but add noise-gate: require >3 distinct hosts reporting p99s for 5m.
sara: documenting decision: squelch p99 for 10m, set noise-gate, create dashboard panel for per-model p95/p99 and kv-cache miss rate. Also add link to runbook.
lee: queries I used (PromQL):
```
# p99 latency per route
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, model))
# kv-cache miss rate
sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) by (model)
```
anya: can we add per-route per-model p99 panels to the Alerting dashboard? Right now we have only global p99 and per-route p95
mike: filing a ticket: INFRA-1427 -> "Add per-route+model p95/p99 panels and kv-cache-miss heatmap" linking to this thread
sara: noted customer impact + mitigation in incident tracker. recommended follow-ups: adjust p99 threshold for chat.completions.default-worker from 1.8s -> 2.0s for 24h while we gather more data, add noise-gating rule, and create alert that splits by model.
lee: I think raising threshold modestly prevents pager churn while we triage. but we must not hide real perf regressions. add a regression detector on rolling 6h baseline relative to control group.
anya: runbook updates: add step to check kv-cache miss rate and fallback split, include commands to apply temporary route split and roll it back.
ops-bot: Pager squelch applied by sara for 10m on alert_id=ALERT-68421. Note: escalations still active.
mike: follow-up immediate tasks assigned: investigate root cause of kv-cache miss spike (possible eviction bug or memory pressure), check model-serving scaling events, and validate batch window heuristics.
sara: handoff to next oncall @mike for long-running investigation. I’m going offline for customer comms. next update in #eng-sre in 30m or on ticket INFRA-1427.
mike: ack. will keep thread updated. current status: mitigation applied, p99 reduced to ~1.6s, no new customer complaints.
lee: after-action item: add automatic per-model alerting so we don't aggregate away model-specific flapping. logging that in INFRA-1427 as subtasks.
anya: suggested retention: keep per-route/model p99s at 15m window for alerts and 5m for dashboard. reduces noise.
sara: thanks everyone. capture notes and we’ll schedule a short post-incident review tomorrow. :thumbsup:
